Joan I died on 29 September 1360 and 'Her possessions were inherited by her son' Philip of Rouvres, who died on 21 November 1361 (Joan I page; the pages opened do not say who held the counties after him). The duchy of 1360 is the royal land, not the county: 'In 1356, King John II of France made the Terre d'Auvergne a Duchy for his third son John, Duke of Berry' and 'the County of Auvergne continued to exist in parallel' (Duchy page); the Berry page: 'his father granted John the newly raised duchies of Berry and Auvergne'. So the county's shape does not change in 1360, and the earlier version of this keyframe, which drew the whole block, is withdrawn (reviewer finding). The Duchy of Berry and Auvergne is a separate state that needs its own dossier.

Cliopatria's 1363..1374 shape (19,677 km2: the whole Auvergne block plus Boulogne) is the Duchy of Auvergne of John, Duke of Berry ('Duke of Auvergne 1360-1416', Berry page infobox) together with the county; the Duchy page keeps them apart: 'the County of Auvergne continued to exist in parallel'. The county held only the remnant round Vic-le-Comte plus Boulogne (about 3,500 km2: a 30 km radius is about 2,800 km2 and Boulogne 706 km2), a factor of about 5.6 smaller than the shape. Area check: the Auvergne page infobox gives 26,013 km2 for the modern region, 'generally regarded as conterminous with the land area of the historical Province of Auvergne'; against the 19,677 km2 block the ratio is 1.32, within a factor of two, so the block is the province (the duchy plus the county), not the county, and against the corrected county the infobox is about 7 times larger. 'Creation of the Royal land of Auvergne (1213)' and 'added it to the Domaine royal in 1213 as Terre royale d'Auvergne' (Duchy page); 'King Philip August linked the majority of the county to the royal territory' and 'the Count held out in Vic-le-Comte' (Auvergne page, second page). Alphonse of Poitiers holds the royal land as an apanage from 1225 ('In 1225, Louis VIII of France granted Poitou and Auvergne to his third son Alfonso', County of Auvergne page) until 1271 ('On Alfonso's death in 1271, Auvergne ... reverted to the royal domain'). The French county page (second page) says the counts kept a small territory in the middle of the Limagne round Vic-le-Comte, its independence guaranteed to Guy II, and that Vic-le-Comte became their new capital (no year given); no page gives a boundary.

region.text: the county of Boulogne, Cliopatria's 706 km2 polygon at Boulogne-sur-Mer

ledger.note: 1260: Cliopatria adds the Boulogne-sur-Mer polygon to the shape. The Boulogne page says that after Matilda II the county 'passed to Matilda's niece, Adelaide of Brabant and her husband William X of Auvergne' (no year given), so the union can be no earlier than Matilda II's death in January 1259 (Matilda II page, second page) and no later than Joan I's 'ruling Countess of Auvergne and Boulogne from 1332 to 1360' (Joan I page); 1260 is Cliopatria's year and no page confirms it. The Boulogne page has an Alberic who 'died in 1284' without issue. The Robert V page opened for this gap does not mention Boulogne or Robert V.

29 September 1360: Joan I dies (infobox 'Died: 29 September 1360') and 'Her possessions were inherited by her son' Philip of Rouvres (the infobox successor is 'Philip of Rouves'; the succession table says Philip III of Boulogne). The county passes to the House of Burgundy's duke; the shape does not change. Philip died on 21 November 1361 and the pages opened do not say who held the counties next. The 1356/1360 Duchy of Auvergne for John, Duke of Berry is the royal land, not the county: 'the County of Auvergne continued to exist in parallel' (Duchy page), so the earlier 1360 gain and 1416 loss of the Terre royale have been withdrawn.

1424: Joan II, Countess of Auvergne and Boulogne from 1394 (infobox 1404), dies ('c. 1424' in the infobox) and 'The counties passed to her cousin, Marie, upon her death in 1424'. Marie I of Auvergne's husband was Bertrand IV of La Tour, whom she married in 1389 (La Tour page: 'married a rich heiress, Marie I, Countess of Auvergne, in 1389'); their son Bertrand V succeeded as 'Count of Auvergne and Boulogne in 1437'. The earlier version of this dossier put the La Tour succession in 1389, which the Joan II page contradicts.

1477: Boulogne passes to Louis XI. 'In 1477, Bertrand II dealt with Louis XI, exchanging the county of Boulogne with the county of Lauragais' and Boulogne was 'eventually annexed to the royal domain itself in 1477.'

1477: the La Tour counts receive the county of Lauragais in the exchange (Boulogne page); Jean III is 'the last medieval Count of Auvergne, Boulogne, and Lauraguais' (La Tour page). The extent of Lauragais is not given by either page.

ledger.note: 1524: Anne de la Tour d'Auvergne dies. She 'was sovereign Countess of Auvergne from 1501 until 1524' and left 'the feudal county of Auvergne' to her niece Catherine de' Medici (Anne page); the senior male line had ended with Jean III on 28 March 1501 (John III page: 'last in the male line of Counts of Auvergne from the La Tour d'Auvergne family'; La Tour page: 'extinct in 1501'). 1524 is the last year the pages hold: the county was not absorbed in 1501, as the earlier version of this dossier drew it (Cliopatria's last shape is 1496-1501), and the Catherine de' Medici page is silent on Auvergne, so the year in which the county merged into the crown is not on any page opened (confidence 1; the successor is the kingdom by default).

notes:
Reworked 2026-10-25 after the eu-10-f review (verdict fail). Main correction: the earlier version folded John of Berry's Duchy of Auvergne (the Terre royale, 1360-1416) into the county, through a 1360 gain from kingdom-of-france and a 1416 loss to house-of-bourbon, and so drew Cliopatria's whole block (19,677 km2) for 56 years where the county held only the Vic-le-Comte remnant plus Boulogne (about 3,500 km2). The Duchy page says the duchy was made in 1356/1360 'while the County of Auvergne continued to exist in parallel', and the Joan I and Joan II pages carry the county through Philip of Rouvres (1360-1361), Joan II (1394 or 1404 to c. 1424, countess beside John of Berry from 1404 per the Berry succession box) and her cousin Marie (1424), never to Berry. Those two events are deleted, house-of-bourbon is no longer a successor, and keyframes 1360 to 1415 are adjusted to the remnant plus Boulogne. The Duchy of Berry and Auvergne (apanage of John, Duke of Berry, 1360-1416) is a separate state that needs its own dossier (suggested slug duchy-of-berry); kingdom-of-france's 1360 loss already names it and house-of-bourbon's 1416 gain names 'Duchy of Auvergne (John, Duke of Berry)'.
Other changes: Vic-le-Comte is the only capital (Riom was occupied by Philip II from 1195); the war starts in 1206 (reviewer); the infobox area is quoted (26,013 km2 for the modern region, ratio 1.32 against the 19,677 km2 block, about 7 against the corrected county); the La Tour succession moves from 1389 to 1424 (Joan II page); the 1260 Boulogne gain now rests on the Boulogne page (passed to Adelaide of Brabant and William X of Auvergne, undated; Matilda II died January 1259); the state now runs to 1524 because Anne was sovereign Countess of Auvergne 1501-1524 (Anne page) and the county was not absorbed in 1501 (John III page: only the male line ended).
Cliopatria reading: the 1206-1351 block (78 cells, 19,726 km2 in 1300) is Puy-de-Dôme, Cantal and Haute-Loire; the Auvergne page gives the county as Puy-de-Dôme, the northern half of Cantal and a small north-western third of Haute-Loire (ratio 0.76 on cells). From 1260 it adds Boulogne-sur-Mer (706 km2), the polygon that is the whole shape from 1440. The row stops 1352-1362 and 1407-1439. The remnant radius (30 km round Vic-le-Comte) is mine; the French page says the counts kept 'a small territory in the middle of the Limagne round Vic-le-Comte'; a gap-filler should open the French Terre d'Auvergne pages for a boundary.
Disagreements between pages: duchy created 1356 or 1360 (Duchy page has both); Bourbon succession to the duchy 1416 or 1426 (not this state's); Alphonse's apanage 1225 (County of Auvergne page) or 1226 (Auvergne page); Joan II countess from 1394 (text) or 1404 (infobox); Anne's death 1524 (Boulogne page, Anne page) against 1512 (La Tour page tree), settled for 1524 by two pages.
Not settled: the founding of the county (confidence 1); the counts of 1361-1394 (Joan II's father John II d. 1394); when and how the union with Boulogne was made (Boulogne page: after Matilda II, undated; kept at Cliopatria's 1260); why Cliopatria drops Boulogne in 1402-1439; the extent of Lauragais and whether Anne kept it; the county's merger into the crown after Catherine de' Medici inherited it in 1524 (no page opened); the Robert V page does not hold the information the review asked for.
Cross-references (not pages): county-of-boulogne is the counterpart of the 1260 gain and needs the matching loss; kingdom-of-france needs a 1213 gain of the Terre royale, a 1477 gain of Boulogne and a 1477 loss of Lauragais, and its 1407 gain of Auvergne cells is the end of the duchy's shape, not this state's. Pages failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counts_of_Boulogne (url_not_found). Gazetteer names needed: Vic-le-Comte and Riom (places), Lauragais (region).
